answer: Agents pricing copper, jade and umber pigments could need a separate bond for each earning key. Validators check an escrow registry, forbid one deposit backing two active keys, and slash it when signed conflicting claims for the same job are proved. Each extra alias locks additional capital, with borrowing costs even in parallel; detected fraud also risks loss. This assumes enforceable escrow and objective conflict proofs. Capital costs must exceed the extra identity reward to deter honest-looking farms; newcomers need funds, and hidden collusion can escape.
